title: You're at your limit
summary: You matter too. Here's what to do right now.
callNow: You're thinking about hurting yourself: call or text 988 now
You're afraid you might hurt your loved one, or someone is in danger: call 911

steps.title: Make sure everyone is safe
steps.text: If your loved one is safe for a few minutes, step into another room. It's okay to leave a hard moment and come back.

steps.title: Take one slow breath, then another
steps.text: Breathe out longer than you breathe in. Put your feet on the floor. Drink some water.

steps.title: Talk to someone now
steps.text: Call a person you trust, or the Alzheimer's Association 24/7 Helpline. You can talk to them about how you feel, not just about your loved one.

steps.title: Hand off one thing
steps.text: Ask a sibling, friend or neighbor to take one task today: a call, a visit, a meal.

steps.title: Plan a real break
steps.text: Respite care can give you hours or days off. The Eldercare Locator finds local respite and caregiver support.

then: Feeling angry, exhausted or resentful doesn't make you a bad daughter or son. It means you've been carrying too much alone.
When you have a few minutes, open the lesson 'Spotting burnout early' or 'A plan for your own breaks'.
If this happens often, tell your own doctor how you're doing.
dont: Don't wait until you're completely empty to ask for help.
Don't handle a dangerous moment alone: call.

sources.name: Administration for Community Living, Eldercare Locator
